gap_candidates.description: Add a canonical append-only event/record family for account-pressure and switching: account_pressure_episode and account_switch_event | Add a governance rule for provider_account_id: either retire it or explicitly define it as provider-native metadata subordinate to stable internal effective_account_id | Add a node_concerns[] / concern_count projection to the Run Graph node state model so concern details are surfaced at node click | Add account_switch_event and account_pressure_episode families to storage-plan.md and Contracts_V0.md | Add execution_role to effective-resolution record, attempt_record, tier_runtime_record or successor, and usage_record
exact_missing_items: Add a canonical append-only event/record family for account-pressure and switching: account_pressure_episode and account_switch_event

account_pressure_episode fields: episode_id, project_id, provider_id, account_id, execution_role?, source_kind, signal_confidence, pressure_kind, projected_remaining?, reset_at?, started_at_utc, updated_at_utc, ended_at_utc?, status

account_switch_event fields: switch_event_id, project_id, provider_id, execution_role?, requested_account_id?, from_account_id?, to_account_id?, switch_reason, decision_kind, source_episode_id?, run_id?, attempt_id?, thread_id?, ts
Add a governance rule for provider_account_id: either retire it or explicitly define it as provider-native metadata subordinate to stable internal effective_account_id
provider_account_id is being normalized in usage/storage-facing docs without a governing rule, so it risks becoming a second shadow routing identity
Add a node_concerns[] / concern_count projection to the Run Graph node state model so concern details are surfaced at node click
Bind concern-rendering to canonical concern record via concern_id, not ad-hoc blocked strings
Align Run Graph command bindings with UI_Command_Catalog.md canonical cmd.runtime.*, cmd.orchestrator.open_in_* variants
Add account_switch_event and account_pressure_episode families to storage-plan.md and Contracts_V0.md
Define the canonical switch-event schema with required fields (old/new effective account, switch_reason, scope, pressure levels, timeline)
Define pressure-episode schema and bind it to History/Ledger/Usage Pressure projections
Add execution_role to effective-resolution record, attempt_record, tier_runtime_record or successor, and usage_record
Add operational-identity blocks to runtime records where side-effectful or externally-scoped actions matter
Operational identity kinds: github_api_account, registry_namespace, kubernetes_context
Ensure GUI inspectors can show requested/effective provider/account identity, requested/effective operational identity, execution role, and selection/switch reason
Add execution_role to the canonical runtime attempt packet in Contracts_V0.md
Contracts_V0.md already has a fairly strong attempt.started packet, but it still does not name execution_role, which is now needed to separate provider/account identity from what the actor was doing
Blocked/degraded reason fields in the effective-resolution record must be normative and explicit
blocked_reason_code is the canonical machine-readable reason; blocked_reason_detail is optional human-readable context
degraded_reason_code and degraded_reason_detail follow the same pattern
Both pairs must appear on the effective-resolution record, not scattered as ad-hoc strings in concern records, HITL events, or attention items
Crosswalk.md §2 routing table must add Primitive:RouteTarget pointing to Contracts_V0.md §route_target and Primitive:OpenSubject pointing to Contracts_V0.md §OpenSubject
These entries should follow the same routing-table pattern as other Crosswalk primitives
Define actor_kind enum and execution_role enum in Contracts_V0.md with initial values to unblock persona resolution, permission scoping, and role-by-provider account overrides
Add both fields to the canonical actor envelope
Use actor_kind in stream events to distinguish overseer, executor, reviewer, corroborator, and observer roles
Define the canonical `object_kind` enum in `Contracts_V0.md`.

The canonical `object_kind` set: conversational/upstream: `thread`, `message`, `wizard`, `usage_event`; runtime/execution: `run`, `node`, `attempt`, `scheduler_pass`, `blocked_episode`, `safe_point`, `remediation`; orchestration rewrite: `feature_seam`, `work_package`, `lane`, `worktree`, `concern`, `promotion`, `graph_patch`, `graph_generation`

`object_id` must use existing canonical ids: `thread_id`, `message_id`, `wizard_id`, `run_id`, `attempt_id`, `scheduler_pass_id`, `blocked_sequence` in `{ run_id, node_id }` scope, `safe_point_id`, `remediation_root_id`, `lane_id`, `worktree_id`, concern/promotion/graph-patch/graph-generation ids when defined
`tier`, `tier_id`, raw widget ids, panel ids, and serialization tokens do not belong in `object_kind`.
If new object families appear, they must be added deliberately, not ad hoc in surface docs.
stale_tokens: raw widget ids as object_kind values
canonical_replacement_hints: effective_account_id is the stable internal identity; provider_account_id should be explicitly subordinate provider-native metadata
object_kind = node | attempt | scheduler_pass | blocked_episode for tier-era pivots
gap_candidates.blocking_reason: Concrete Plans/** document requires content reconciliation vs transfer obligation.
